issue.title: [INKWAVE][Perf] Mobile post stack permanently pins two full-resolution RGBA16F composer buffers
issue.body:
## Main SHA

`fc057af9baac421ec707504f4637e2ed8824a444`

Current `main` was re-fetched immediately before investigation.

## Target device / state

- iPhone/iPad/Android WebGL builds, especially the default HIGH setting after mobile effective-quality caps.
- Also affects desktop HIGH/ULTRA at higher device pixel ratios.
- Present in menus/attract, live battle, pause/results, and any other state where the main composer remains allocated.
- This is persistent GPU memory, independent of the separate paint/shadow/mural/PropKit/texlib render-target findings.

## Root cause

`inkwave-public/src/core/renderer.js` always constructs the main post stack around a full-resolution half-float render target:

```js
const pr = Math.min(window.devicePixelRatio || 1, q.pixelRatio, mobileCap) * this.dynScale;
...
const samples = this.mobile.touch ? 0 : (q.msaa || 0);
const rt = new THREE.WebGLRenderTarget(w * pr, h * pr, {
  type: THREE.HalfFloatType,
  samples
});
const comp = (this.composer = new EffectComposer(r, rt));
comp.setPixelRatio(pr);
comp.setSize(w, h);
```

The vendored Three.js `EffectComposer` immediately clones the supplied target:

```js
this.renderTarget1 = renderTarget;
this.renderTarget2 = renderTarget.clone();
this.writeBuffer = this.renderTarget1;
this.readBuffer = this.renderTarget2;
```

so the base composer permanently owns **two** full-resolution `HalfFloatType` ping-pong targets.

Mobile effective quality disables MSAA, GTAO and bloom:

```js
q = Object.freeze({
  ...base,
  ...
  msaa: 0,
  ao: false,
  bloom: false,
  pixelRatio: Math.min(base.pixelRatio, mobile.ios ? 1.2 : 1.35),
});
```

but it does not change the composer target type or eliminate one of the two RGBA16F buffers. The buffers therefore remain allocated even when the expensive HDR-oriented optional passes are absent and ScreenFX is idle/disabled.

## Code-derived memory lower bound

A four-channel half-float color buffer is 8 bytes/pixel (4 × 16-bit). Two composer color targets therefore cost a guaranteed color-only lower bound of:

`drawingWidth × drawingHeight × 16 bytes`

where `drawingWidth = CSS width × effective pixel ratio` and likewise for height.

Examples from the code's own pixel-ratio rules, before counting depth attachments, driver padding, other post-pass targets, shadows, paint, FX, mural, PropKit, etc.:

- 744×1133 CSS px at iOS default HIGH cap 1.2: about **18.5 MiB** color-only.
- 800×1280 CSS px at non-iOS touch HIGH cap 1.35: about **28.5 MiB** color-only.
- 1920×1080 desktop HIGH at PR 1.5: about **71.2 MiB** color-only.
- 1920×1080 desktop ULTRA at PR 2.0: about **126.6 MiB** color-only.

LOW reduces the pixel ratio, but it still keeps the same two half-float targets.

## Reproduction / measurement

After boot on current main:

```js
const c = __inkwave.R.composer;
const a = c.renderTarget1, b = c.renderTarget2;
({
  a: [a.width, a.height, a.texture.type],
  b: [b.width, b.height, b.texture.type],
  colorMiBLowerBound: (a.width * a.height + b.width * b.height) * 8 / 1048576,
  quality: __inkwave.settings.quality,
  mobile: __inkwave.mobile,
});
```

Then compare HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW on a touch device. Even when `__inkwave.R.gtao === null`, `__inkwave.R.bloom === null`, and `__inkwave.screenfx.pass.enabled === false`, both full-resolution half-float targets remain.

For GPU confirmation, capture a WebGL/Metal/GPU memory trace or browser GPU resource capture before and after replacing the mobile composer target with a lower-precision/direct path.

## Expected

Mobile quality presets that disable MSAA/GTAO/bloom should have a post stack whose persistent memory footprint is proportional to the passes actually needed, and should not reserve high-precision ping-pong storage unless the active grade/ScreenFX path demonstrably requires it.

## Actual

Two full-resolution RGBA16F-equivalent color targets remain resident for the base composer on every quality/device path. On tablet-sized touch viewports the color-only lower bound is already tens of MiB at the default HIGH mobile cap.

## Performance / resource impact

- Adds persistent GPU memory pressure on iOS/Android on top of paint, shadows, mural, PropKit, texlib and FX allocations.
- Higher GPU memory pressure increases the risk of browser/WebGL context loss and memory eviction on constrained devices.
- Full-resolution half-float ping-pong also doubles color-buffer bandwidth for every composer pass that swaps buffers.
- The cost persists in non-battle/menu states because the composer is a page-lifetime renderer resource.
- Desktop HIGH/ULTRA can reserve substantially larger buffers at 1.5–2.0 render density.

## Fix direction

Profile visual requirements first, then choose the cheapest valid path per effective quality:

- For touch/mobile presets where GTAO/bloom are disabled, test an `UnsignedByteType` composer target if Grade/ScreenFX output remains visually equivalent.
- If ScreenFX is idle and the remaining chain can be fused, consider a single post target/direct render path rather than unconditional ping-pong.
- If HDR is truly required for active ScreenFX, allocate/switch to the higher-precision path only while needed, or use a lower-resolution screen-FX intermediate.
- Keep current HalfFloat ping-pong on desktop/high-quality paths only where measured visual benefit justifies the memory/bandwidth.

Do not change gameplay simulation or render resolution as part of this fix.

## Regression / acceptance criteria

- Record `renderTarget1/2` dimensions/type and a GPU memory capture on LOW/MEDIUM/HIGH touch profiles before/after.
- Mobile idle/menu and normal battle post-stack persistent color memory is materially lower than the current two-RGBA16F baseline.
- Grade/tone mapping, FXAA, damage/lens ink, swim/special/flood ScreenFX and color output remain visually equivalent within agreed image-diff tolerance.
- Dynamic resolution changes and orientation/resize do not leak old targets.
- Desktop HIGH/ULTRA retain HDR precision where required.
- No regression in WebGL context stability or post-processing output.

## Duplicate check

Checked open/closed GitHub issues and ChatGPT Library `/INKWAVE Issue Queue` against current main using `EffectComposer`, `HalfFloatType`, `RGBA16F`, post-processing ping-pong and mobile GPU-memory queries. No existing item covers this composer-buffer allocation.
